lore_anchors.definition: A spiritual herb that grows near demon beast lairs, nourished by ambient demonic energy. Higher-grade beasts produce more potent herbs but make harvesting them far more dangerous.
A high-tier demon beast roughly equivalent to a late Core Formation or early Nascent Soul cultivator. Encountering one is a life-threatening event even for veteran cultivators.
A precious, one-time-use artifact created by sealing a fraction of a magic treasure's power into a talisman. Extremely valuable to Qi Condensation cultivators.

The third major cultivation realm. A Core Formation cultivator possesses far greater magical power, lifespan, and social status than Foundation Establishment cultivators, but still faces life-threatening risks from high-grade demon beasts.
A common storage medium in the cultivation world for recording text, techniques, and diagrams. Read by injecting spiritual sense into the slip.
The dangerous, outer regions of the Chaotic Star Sea, home to high-grade demon beasts and valuable resources. A classic frontier hunting ground for rogue cultivators.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li look disappointed after scanning the jade slip?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because the Thousand Leaf Dew is actually Companion Herb sap from an eighth-grade demon beast's lair. That makes harvesting it a near-suicidal mission, not a simple herb-gathering trip.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the white-robed figure hiding in the painting?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A second cultivator working with Li Xun, likely a high-level spy or guard. He watched the entire conversation and suspects that Han Li sensed his presence despite his concealment technique.
Probably. Han Li pays 5,000 spirit stones for it without haggling and seems satisfied with the purchase. In the Mortal Stream, any resource he deliberately acquires usually becomes relevant later.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li refuse Li Xun's invitation to hunt in a group?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He does not trust Li Xun or any unknown cultivators. Group hunting in the Mortal Stream is often a cover for betrayal, ambush, or exploitation. Han Li's standard strategy is to go solo or with assets he controls completely.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is this chapter setting up something big?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes. The eighth-grade beast, the agate horn, and the hidden observer are all flags planted for future arcs. Mortal Stream novels build tension through logistics, not explosions—this chapter is laying the foundation for a much larger conflict.
